clauses.source_paraphrase: While preparing the expert declaration in the music-publishers' copyright lawsuit, an Anthropic lawyer used Claude to format a citation to a real statistics article. The citation retained credible journal/year/link details but invented the article title and author names. A legitimate underlying paper existed; the faulty attribution was not evidence that the entire article or source URL was invented.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A generated legal citation must preserve the identity of the linked source at the accuracy needed for formal reliance.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: A plausible citation to a real article entered the expert declaration with invented identifying fields. The correct URL did not make the title and authors fit for a court-facing source reference.

Claude’s formatted citation attributed the real article to the wrong authors and title while retaining the correct journal and URL, making the source identity materially false in the filed declaration.

Incorrect Claude citation metadata was submitted after some narrower bibliographic corrections. The court's independent verification requirement was not fulfilled; whether the partial corrections were accepted as sufficient completion of that requirement remains unverified.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Before filing, the legal team read the real paper and made some bibliographic corrections but did not catch the false title and authors. Counsel later acknowledged responsibility for the insufficient review. This is a separate human checking failure, not proof that the model had authority to certify a legal filing.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A human citation check must compare every material bibliographic field with the authoritative source when the result will be formally submitted.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The legal team performed a narrower manual cite-check and corrected some bibliographic fields; that activity cannot itself be described as an omitted check. The later court order identifies a separate requirement for lead-trial-counsel verification and certification that had not occurred. The court-order clause below supports the finding about that distinct unmet duty.

clauses.source_paraphrase: At the May 2025 hearing the opposing counsel challenged the citation. Magistrate Judge Susan van Keulen required an explanation, held that the applicable verification/certification requirements were not satisfied and struck the affected expert declaration paragraph. The court's order and counsel's acknowledgements are later responses to the previously submitted citation.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Where a governing legal process requires a defined personal verification and certification before submission, a narrower informal check cannot substitute for completing and evidencing the required verification.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The court identified a specific required verification and certification step and expressly found that it had not occurred before the reliance-bearing filing; the court then struck the affected paragraph.
